display.title: Episode 490: The Sound of the Shofar (Shabbos Mevarchim Elul)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi's Shabbos Mevarchim Elul show: the King in the Field, Shema with a yeshiva boy, and a story of a farm boy's bugle that explains why we blow the shofar.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week of Shabbos Mevarchim Elul 5751. Uncle Yossi teaches two words for the new month, Melech BaSadeh, 'the King in the field'. He retells the Alter Rebbe's parable from Likkutei Torah: when a king returns home, the people go out to greet him in the fields, and there anyone may approach him and he grants every request with a shining face. In Elul Hashem is just as close, so children should make a long wish list for body and soul, with Moshiach at the top. After the Hakochainik march, a yeshiva boy leads the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time is 'The Sound of the Shofar': after fires keep destroying their village, the villagers send a farm boy to the big city, where the fire chief shows him how he blows a bugle from a tall tower. Back home the boy blows his new bugle while the houses burn, until the chief explains that the bugle is only an alarm telling people to run for water. So too, the shofar wakes us to act with teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah. The show ends with a call to enroll in a yeshiva for the new year.
display.lesson: The shofar is an alarm, not the cure: it wakes us to act with teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah, while in Elul Hashem, the King in the field, is close to everyone.

date.note: 'This coming Shabbos is Shabbos Mevarchim Elul' (23 Av 5751 = 3 Aug 1991); ep. 491 has Rosh Chodesh Elul on Shabbos, which fits 5751; Tuesday broadcast.

advisories.note: Fires burn down village homes; no one is hurt.
